w: At the northeast tip of Long Point, this white square tower marks the edge of the entrance to Provincetown Harbor with an occulting green light, visible 8 nautical miles out. In poor visibility its fog horn sounds every 15 seconds, seeming to call out to its near-identical neighbor, Wood End Light.
s: A fog horn calling to its twin, Wood End Light
_facts: White square tower at the northeast tip of Long Point
Green occulting light, visible range 8 nautical miles
Fog horn sounds a two-second blast every 15 seconds
Marks the entrance to Provincetown Harbor

w: Built 1907-1910 to mark the Pilgrims' actual first landfall in 1620 - Provincetown, not Plymouth - and the signing of the Mayflower Compact in its harbor. At 252 feet 7.5 inches, this granite campanile is the tallest all-granite structure in the United States.
s: Where the Pilgrims really landed first
_facts: Commemorates the Pilgrims' 1620 landfall and the Mayflower Compact signing
252 feet 7.5 inches tall
Tallest all-granite structure in the United States

w: First lit in 1816 and rebuilt in 1876 as a 45-foot iron-plated tower, this lighthouse sits at the edge of Cape Cod, reachable only by a 45-minute walk over sand or by four-wheel-drive with a park permit. The American Lighthouse Foundation now rents out its keeper's buildings for overnight stays.
s: A lighthouse reached by a 45-minute sand walk
_facts: Original tower lit 1816, rebuilt 1876 at 45 feet
Iron-plated tower with a keeper's dwelling
Reached by a 45-minute walk over sand or 4WD with a permit
Keeper's buildings rented for overnight stays

w: This Methodist church on Commercial Street lost its congregation to a new building in 1955 and has changed hands several times since. It is now the home of the Provincetown Public Library, listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
s: A church that became the town library
_facts: Located at 356 Commercial Street
Congregation moved to a new building in 1955
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places
Now home to the Provincetown Public Library

w: Built in 1847 to a Benjamin Hallett design for a congregation founded in 1829, this Greek Revival meeting house was raised without its telescoping, Greek-ornamented tower - added later. That steeple is now the only one left standing in Provincetown, a landmark for sailors entering the harbor.
s: The last steeple standing in Provincetown
_facts: Built 1847, designed by Benjamin Hallett
Congregation founded 1829
Tower added later; the only surviving steeple in Provincetown
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972

w: Founded in 1914 to collect and exhibit work by Cape Cod artists, PAAM's holdings span Impressionists, Modernists and Futurists alongside more traditional styles. Renamed from the Provincetown Art Association in 1970, it now represents roughly 700 member artists and holds over 4,000 works.
s: A century of Cape Cod art, since 1914
_facts: Founded August 22, 1914 as the Provincetown Art Association
Renamed Provincetown Art Association and Museum in 1970
